clue.text: Sounds like, a long queue for this quantity

indicators.note: the clue says outright that what follows is to be judged by how it sounds when spoken

parts.note: a very long queue might mean a hundred people wait, a 'hundred wait'

explanation.surface: A riddle asking which unit of measure sounds like waiting in a very long line.
explanation.walkthrough: A hundredweight is an old British unit of weight (112 lb). Spoken, it matches 'hundred wait', the wait of a hundred-strong queue.
explanation.definitionFit: A hundredweight is an imperial unit of mass, so it is a measured amount.

clue.text: "Wait a moment'" as: stage-hand might have, said

definitions.meaning: a call to stop and be patient
a theatre hand in charge of horses on stage might tell someone to grasp the animals

explanation.surface: A theatre worker asking someone to pause for a second.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom for 'be patient' is read literally as an order to grip horses, as a stage-hand handling animals in a show might give.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom tells someone to slow down; literally it is an order to restrain mounts.

clue.text: Dig a dug out in the north-east

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go inside the compass abbreviation

parts.note: NE is the abbreviation for north-east

indicators.note: the letters of dug are put out of order

explanation.surface: Excavating a bunker in the north-east of England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dig' looks like excavation to match the dug-out; it is the definition, a prod with the elbow. 'out' scrambles the fodder and 'in' places the result inside the compass pair.
explanation.definitionFit: A dig is a poke with the elbow, a prod.

clue.text: Dora's later, disposition to the character of Copperfield

indicators.note: a disposition is an arrangement, so the letters are set out anew

explanation.surface: Dora's later temperament compared with a figure in Dickens's novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disposition' rearranges DORAS LATER. Dora Spenlow is David Copperfield's first wife, a decoy from the same novel; Rosa Dartle is Steerforth's scarred companion.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosa Dartle is a figure in Dickens's David Copperfield.

clue.text: Trickle forward movement

definitions.meaning: a thin, slow flow of liquid
in football, advancing the ball with small touches past opponents

explanation.surface: A slow drip edging ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin stream and running with a ball at one's feet share this word.

clue.text: Brought out of a grave situation'

definitions.text: Brought out of a grave situation

parts.words: Brought out of a grave situation
parts.note: reads as rescued from serious trouble, but means taken from a burial plot

explanation.surface: Someone rescued from serious trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grave' looks like serious; it is the burial place.
explanation.definitionFit: Disinterred bodies are dug up from their burial place.

clue.text: Open wide — something that needs stopping, note

parts.note: a gap is a hole to be stopped or plugged
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: An instruction to open one's mouth, with a reminder about a hole needing a plug.
explanation.definitionFit: To gape is to stand open or to stare open-mouthed.

clue.text: Battle square

definitions.meaning: the 1805 naval victory of Nelson over the French and Spanish
the London public square with Nelson's Column

explanation.surface: A fight in a town square.
explanation.walkthrough: Trafalgar Square in London is named after the battle.
explanation.definitionFit: Nelson's 1805 sea fight gave its name to a London plaza.

clue.text: Castaway fliers on 'and off course?

parts.note: robins are birds, things that fly
taken as written

indicators.note: the letters of course are put off their order

explanation.surface: Shipwrecked birds driven off their route.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges COURSE into CRUSOE. Defoe's Robinson Crusoe is the archetypal castaway.
explanation.definitionFit: Defoe's hero was marooned on a desert island.

clue.text: How relieved she was in 1900 !

parts.note: reads as a woman's relief, but refers to a besieged South African town whose siege was lifted in 1900 during the Boer War

explanation.surface: A woman sighing with relief at the turn of the century.
explanation.walkthrough: The Relief of Ladysmith (February 1900) ended a long siege in the Boer War. 'She' points to LADY, and the town is treated as a woman who was 'relieved'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Natal town besieged by the Boers was famously relieved by British forces in 1900.

clue.text: Top artist has party in Spanish gallery

parts.note: PRA is President of the Royal Academy, the head of Britain's leading art body
a do is an informal word for a party

explanation.surface: A leading painter throws a party at a Madrid art museum.
explanation.definitionFit: The Prado is the national art museum in Madrid.

clue.text: To strive, to seek, to find, and not to ——" (Tennyson)

definitions.text: To strive, to seek, to find, and not to ——" (Tennyson)

parts.words: To strive, to seek, to find, and not to
parts.note: the closing line of Tennyson's poem Ulysses, with its final word left blank for the solver to supply

explanation.surface: A famous line of Victorian poetry with its last word missing.
explanation.walkthrough: The line ends Tennyson's 'Ulysses' (1842): the blank is the verb meaning give in.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing word of the quotation means to give way or surrender.

clue.text: Dull sound of success on the river

definitions.meaning: a thud, the noise of something heavy knocking
in Oxford and Cambridge ... races, a crew succeeds by catching and touching the boat ahead

explanation.surface: A rowing crew's triumph marked by a muffled thud.
explanation.walkthrough: In bumps races at Oxford and Cambridge, boats start in a line and score by catching and touching the boat in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a muffled thud and a rowing win where one boat touches another share this word.

clue.text: Egypt's handmaid returns this garment

indicators.note: the name of the handmaid is to be read from its end back to its start

parts.note: Iras is one of Cleopatra's attendants in Shakespeare's Antony and Cleopatra, and Cleopatra is called 'Egypt' there

explanation.surface: A servant of the Egyptian queen brings back a piece of clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: In Antony and Cleopatra Shakespeare calls Cleopatra 'Egypt'; her maids are Iras and Charmian. 'returns' turns IRAS round.
explanation.definitionFit: A sari is a draped robe worn by women of South Asia.

clue.text: Assemble a side and act so as to be in league

indicators.note: to assemble is to put parts together, so the letters are built into a new order

explanation.surface: A team getting together to act as part of a sporting league.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Assemble' rearranges ASIDE and ACTSO. 'league' looks sporting; it means alliance.
explanation.definitionFit: To be associated is to be connected or allied with others.

clue.text: Deposit on ground at Badminton perhaps

definitions.text: Deposit on ground at Badminton perhaps

parts.words: Deposit on ground at Badminton perhaps
parts.note: describes a rider being thrown off at a famous horse trials event, not a shuttlecock game

explanation.surface: Someone putting something down on the court at a badminton match.
explanation.walkthrough: Badminton is the English estate that hosts the Badminton Horse Trials; 'Badminton' tempts one towards the racket sport, but the falls there are from horses.
explanation.definitionFit: To throw a rider from the saddle is to land them on the turf.

clue.text: Lady in earshot perhaps

indicators.note: signals that the letters might be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: A woman who may be within hearing distance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges IN EARSHOT. Hortensia is a woman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Hortensia is a female forename, so a woman.

clue.text: Shapes of: things to come ?

definitions.meaning: plans or intentions, things one has in mind for the future

explanation.surface: A question about the forms that the future will take.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls H. G. Wells's 'The Shape of Things to Come'.
explanation.definitionFit: Patterns are forms, and schemes are plans for the future: both are this word.

clue.text: Was in 'the front, but after damage moved noisily:

indicators.note: one piece is placed following the other, so the leading piece comes second

parts.note: to hurt is to damage or injure
to be in front is to have led

explanation.surface: A leader who was hit came crashing along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' places the leading piece second, against the clue's order; 'Was in the front' is a past-tense phrase for being ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: To hurtle is to rush along with great speed and clatter.

clue.text: Take first step towards a change in station'

definitions.text: Take first step towards a change in station

parts.words: Take first step towards a change in station
parts.note: reads as rising in social rank, but means getting off at a railway stop to change trains

explanation.surface: Beginning a climb in social standing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'station' suggests social position; it is a railway station, where changing trains begins with getting off.
explanation.definitionFit: Stepping off a railway carriage is the start of switching to another one.

clue.text: Wherein the Highland fling might shake things up?:

definitions.text: Wherein the Highland fling might shake things up?

parts.words: Wherein the Highland fling might shake things up
parts.note: the Scottish dance makes the kilt's purse bounce, jumbling whatever is carried in it

explanation.surface: A question about what gets jostled during a lively Scottish dance.
explanation.walkthrough: A sporran is the pouch worn at the front of a kilt; dancing a Highland fling shakes its contents.
explanation.definitionFit: A kilt wearer carries belongings in this pouch, which jumps about as they dance.

clue.text: Get up to be prepared

definitions.meaning: a military order to stand ready for action

explanation.surface: Rising so as to be ready.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldiers ordered to their posts stand ready; the phrase also means to rise.

clue.text: Water-grass of unusual hue round the, Orient

indicators.note: the colour word goes around the letter for the East

parts.note: red is a colour or hue
the Orient is the East, abbreviated E

explanation.surface: An oddly coloured grass growing near water in the East.
explanation.definitionFit: A reed is a tall grass-like plant growing in wet places.

clue.text: View 'before returning from Sicily

indicators.note: the word for before is read back to front

parts.note: ante is Latin for before, as in ante-room

explanation.surface: A sight seen before heading home from a Sicilian holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns ANTE round. The volcano is the great view from Sicily, which 'from Sicily' places.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sicilian volcano dominates the island's skyline as a famous sight.

clue.text: Headless champion 'embrace 'ing bull

indicators.note: the word for champion loses its first letter

parts.note: a winner is a champion

explanation.surface: A beheaded champion wrestling with a bull.
explanation.walkthrough: On an archery or darts target, the inner is the ring surrounding the bull's-eye, so 'embracing bull' is the definition, not a wrestling bout.
explanation.definitionFit: On a target, the ring closest to the centre surrounds the bullseye.

clue.text: Love and' one: man could be the making of her

indicators.note: the pieces may be rearranged to produce the name

parts.note: love is nil, the letter O in tennis scoring
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A romance and a single man might make a woman's life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be the making of' rearranges O, I and MAN. Naomi is Ruth's mother-in-law in the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: Naomi is a female name, so the pronoun refers to her.

clue.text: Daisy alias Miss Bronte?

definitions.meaning: Daisy ... is the song 'A Bicycle Built for Two'
Charlotte, Emily and Anne Brontë published as Currer, Ellis and Acton under this surname

explanation.surface: Asking whether a woman named Daisy is a pen-name of one of the Brontës.
explanation.definitionFit: The Brontë sisters' shared pen-surname is also the surname in the song title 'Daisy ___'.

clue.text: Follow directions and prosecute

parts.note: E and N are the compass points East and North
to sue is to take legal action against

explanation.surface: Obeying instructions and taking someone to court.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensue is to come after as a result.

clue.text: They go: on increasing

parts.note: things added on that make a total larger

explanation.surface: Things that keep growing without end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go on' means are attached, not continue.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra pieces tacked on make the whole bigger.

clue.text: Players' well synchronized eventually

definitions.meaning: musicians all keeping to the beat together
sooner or later, when the moment comes

explanation.surface: Musicians finally getting their timing right.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, the phrase says every player is in good time, playing together.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means at the proper moment; literally it means everyone keeping tempo.
